impl.summary:
#374 is fixed in one commit, 07fdc31d, on branch fix/374-sdk-never-reads-another-providers-key in /tmp/wt-374. It sits on aab1f210 and is not pushed. The defect was wider than the issue said. Every provider on api anthropic-messages was affected: 14 catalog providers (fireworks, minimax, opencode, vercel-ai-gateway, kimi-coding, the Xiaomi providers and others) plus any models.json gateway. When one of them resolved no key of its own, the anthropic SDK (0.102.0 locked) read ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN itself. With neither variable set it ran its own credential chain: ANTHROPIC_PROFILE, workload identity federation, and the active profile on disk, all bound to that provider's base_url. A gateway that authenticated with its own header still received the user's Anthropic key next to that header. L14 was ours: the OAuth and Copilot branches passed api_key="", and the SDK sent that as an empty x-api-key header beside the bearer. What changed: - providers/_anthropic_client.py: every client is now built on the AelixAsyncAnthropic subclass. It always passes the SDK an explicit credential, so the SDK reads no credential env var and runs no chain. Afterwards it stores exactly what the caller gave, so None or "" means no x-api-key header at all. copy() and with_options() go through the same subclass. Header validation accepts Authorization, x-api-key and cf-aig-authorization in any letter case. create_async_client gains an auth_token parameter. - providers/anthropic.py: a new _resolve_request_auth runs before any client exists. It takes the caller's key, else get_env_api_key(model.provider), else ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN as a bearer, but only for provider anthropic and only when there is no auth header. The OAuth decision now reads the resolved key. With no key and no auth header the request is never sent and the turn ends with pi's 'No API key for provider:

'. The OAuth and Copilot branches pass api_key=None, and Copilot no longer writes 'Bearer None'. - providers/_google_client.py: the Gemini factory refuses a call with no key, because google-genai has no 'no key' value. The Vertex factory refuses a call that has no key, no project and no location. - Docs: new ADR-0254; dated notes in ADR-0045, 0052, 0203 and 0251; README rows; the models-json and providers-and-models guides and their bundled copies; a CHANGELOG [Unreleased] Security entry; the runtime_bootstrap docstring. Two existing tests pinned api_key=="" and now pin None. Six line citations were re-anchored. Unchanged: the built-in anthropic provider still sends ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (with ANTHROPIC_OAUTH_TOKEN taking precedence), the OAuth bearer flows still work, and a library caller that skips the harness still gets the provider's own env key.

owner_decisions: Vertex ADC stays ambient for any provider whose api is google-vertex, including a custom baseUrl, which receives the Google access token. This matches pi. The owner may prefer to scope ADC to provider google-vertex, the same way ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN is now scoped to anthropic.

The anthropic SDK's own credential chain (ANTHROPIC_PROFILE, workload identity federation, the SDK's active profile on disk) is no longer used, for provider anthropic too. It was never documented and it ran against every anthropic-messages host. pi supports federation for anthropic only. Porting it is filed as a follow-up rather than kept implicitly.

ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN is kept as a bearer for provider anthropic, but last in line: only when no key and no auth header resolved. That preserves aab1f210's effective order. pi tries it before ANTHROPIC_OAUTH_TOKEN and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.

The adapter falls back to get_env_api_key(model.provider), like the sibling adapters, so library use without the harness keeps working. pi's adapter does no env lookup; its harness does. A side effect: ANTHROPIC_OAUTH_TOKEN now also counts for a direct library call to anthropic.
'No API key for provider' arrives as the stream's error event, not as a synchronous raise like pi's streamSimple. The aelix adapter is a single async generator for both stream paths.
ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS, OPENAI_ORG_ID and OPENAI_PROJECT_ID are still read by the SDKs and reach custom hosts. This matches pi's SDKs, and they are not credentials by design. Left unchanged.

blocking.title: Sabotage no test catches: dropping the auth_token re-assignment in AelixAsyncAnthropic.__init__ stays green, and it reopens the leak on an SDK version the pin allows
blocking.detail: packages/aelix-ai/src/aelix_ai/providers/_anthropic_client.py: removing only `self.auth_token = token` (the lane's own S3 survivor) passes tests/providers + tests/oauth (1119 passed). The lane and ADR-0254 section 4 call it redundant with the "" sentinel, but that holds only on the locked anthropic 0.102.0. packages/aelix-ai/pyproject.toml allows anthropic>=0.40,<1.0. I ran the committed module against anthropic 0.40.0. With the line, nothing is read from the environment. Without it, the wrapper sends ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN as `Authorization: Bearer` on every request that goes out: on its own, and as a second Authorization next to a gateway's own header. The adapter guard does not help here, because a request with a key or an auth header passes the guard. So the guard the ADR keeps 'for the older SDKs the range allows' is load-bearing and unpinned. The other survivor (no "" sentinel, S30) is a true equivalent: it measured harmless on both 0.102 and 0.40. Fix (small), either: (a) add a row that wraps AsyncAnthropic.__init__ to copy ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN (and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) into self.* after the real init, as 0.40 does, then assert the factory's client has api_key/auth_token None and sends no bearer or x-api-key; or (b) raise the floor to the measured version (anthropic>=0.102) and say so in ADR-0254 section 4.

#131 is fixed in one commit, 5f7051fa, on /tmp/wt-131 (parent aab1f210). It is not pushed.

`discover install` now works out what an entry's source is from the catalog before the installer sees it. Before, it passed the raw source to classify_target, which reads it relative to the process cwd. The new function is extension_catalog.resolve_entry_source:
(1) A path-shaped source becomes an absolute path. Path-shaped means it starts with ./ ../ / ~ or a backslash, contains / or \, has a drive prefix, or ends in an archive suffix such as .whl, .tar.gz or .zip. A relative one resolves against the directory of the LOCAL catalog file (a bare absolute path or a file:// URL), never the cwd.
(2) A relative source is refused, naming the entry and the catalog, when the catalog is https, git, or registered at a location that is itself relative.
(3) A path that does not exist is refused. It is never retried as a package name.
(4) A package spec goes through unchanged, except in two cases: a file of exactly that name beside the local catalog is refused as ambiguous ("write ./name"), and so is one in the cwd, which the installer would install instead. The cwd case is checked by asking classify_target and requiring its answer to match the catalog's.
(5) URL and VCS specs, and anything typed on the CLI, keep their old meaning. classify_target itself is untouched.

CatalogEntry has a new catalog_location field (not serialized, not compared). The Resolved line now shows the absolute spec and, when it differs, what the catalog said.

`extension index --relative` now writes ./ or ../ POSIX paths measured from the directory the catalog FILE is written to. Absolute paths are still the default. Catalogs written by older versions, which have bare wheel filenames, still install because of the archive-suffix rule.

Docs: a new ADR-0255; a dated amendment to ADR-0188 section 2; a decisions README row for 0255 (there was no 0188 row); docs/guides/private-catalog.md and its bundled copy (a new "Relative paths" section and a rewritten "About --relative"); a CHANGELOG [Unreleased] Security entry; and updated docstrings.

What pi does: pi has no extension catalog (remote-catalog-provider.ts is a model catalog). Its package-manager.ts parseSource treats any source without an npm:/git:/http(s):/ssh: prefix as a local path, and getBaseDirForScope resolves it against the settings file's scope directory (the agent dir, or cwd/.pi). So pi never reaches a registry without an explicit npm: prefix. Aelix has no such prefix (a bare name is a package), so the equivalent guarantee here is that a path-shaped source never goes to an index.

impl.summary: #177 is fixed in one commit: 33b6c43f on branch fix/177-tool-lines-reach-the-terminal-sanitised in /tmp/wt-177. Its parent is main aab1f210, and main has not moved. Not pushed. Every string tui/render.py draws that came from the model, a tool, a provider, an extension or a session file now goes through aelix_ai.utils.terminal_text.safe_for_terminal. There are four shapes. (1) Header rows: tool name, path, bash command, and the compact-args summary including its keys. Each control character becomes a space. render_tool_call_line strips the name and the summary itself, because the live and replay paths both draw through it. The name is capped at 80 cells, and the path at 160 cells from the front so the file name stays. (2) Tool output: card and error bodies, diffs, the edit tool details.diff and the /expand store. Whole ANSI sequences go first, using a port of pi's ansiRegex (pi's getTextOutput rule), then the remaining controls. Newlines and tabs are kept. _truncate_lines strips before it measures. (3) Prose: reasoning, the answer and a custom message body. Stripped per character, so stripping each delta gives the same result as stripping the whole text. (4) Error lines use safe_error_for_terminal. _reported_error stays raw for the #189 dedup. component_to_text keeps the SGR colours and replaces leftover controls in place. The user echo map became safe_for_terminal in SPACE mode, which adds BiDi and the line separators. The regex differs from pi's in two ways: an OSC body cannot cross a newline, and it stops at the next terminator, because pi's lazy form is quadratic (measured). Docs: an ADR-0112 dated amendment, an extension-authoring guide note plus its bundled copy, and a CHANGELOG Unreleased Security entry. Citations into render.py were relocated with --fix. repl.py cited the edited custom-message block and was re-pointed by hand.

MCP, extension and pack tools now ask before they run in default and are blocked in plan, which fixes #188. It is one commit, 4a5d208d, on main aab1f210 in /tmp/wt-188, not pushed. How it works now: the gate no longer checks the eight bare names in _MUTATING. It looks up the tool object the loop will run (the last tool with that name in event.context.tools, the same rule as loop.py) and asks a new module, tools/provenance.py, whether aelix built that object. Aelix's own factories mark what they build: read, grep, find, ls and aelix_status are read-only, bash is bash, write and edit are write, agent is delegation.
